correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the rotations are characteristic because any generator of a cyclic subgroup of order n must be a rotation. The presentation then gives exactly the automorphisms (a,b) acting by ai on rotations and ai+b on reflections. Pairing with r fixes all the rotation images using one unit u, and the reflection images define a permutation π by injectivity. Interpolation at reflections i,j asks for a unit a with a(i−j)=π(i)−π(j) modulo n. At each p^e a common capped valuation t<e reduces this to division of units modulo p^(e−t); any lift is a unit. At t=e there is no restriction. CRT combines the choices. Mixed pairs impose no coupling because a=u fixes the rotation and the freely chosen b fixes the reflection. Composition is coordinatewise. Each congruence relation modulo p^k is preserved in both directions. At k=e this forces the p^e output to factor through the p^e input, so the CRT factors are independent; the lower congruence levels yield precisely the rooted p-ary tree automorphisms. The independent child permutations at (p^e−1)/(p−1) internal nodes give the stated order. The automorphism subgroup has size nφ(n), and taking u=1 and π(i)=−i gives a nonhomomorphic local map for every n≥3. The order-two and Klein-four boundaries follow directly from fixing the identity and being injective. Independent enumeration of all set permutations for n=3,4 gave respectively 12 and 16 two-local maps, agreeing at the level of sets, not just counts.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker's enumeration of all maps reaches only n=1,2,3; its larger checks concern proposed maps and counts. Neither finite check proves the theorem for unbounded n.

evidence: Klin–Kovács covers rational circulants and cyclic congruence block structures by generalized wreath products. Grech–Kisielewicz characterizes abelian permutation groups. The available information for Yu–Pan concerns primitive holomorph types; full text was not obtained.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Cyclic block structures cover technology behind the reflection factor. Neither abelian nor primitive permutation-group scope directly covers the stated intransitive full action.

evidence: The affine action on the reflection labels has gcd-of-difference pair-orbits, consistent with the established cyclic block structure. Mixed interpolation requires the separate observation that the translation is free even after the rotation multiplier is fixed.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing the 2-closures on the two invariant domains individually does not in general give their product on the combined domain. The mixed orbit calculation is the extra mathematical content, not an arithmetic reformulation of the reflection factor.

evidence: Molnár–Šemrl's 'local' condition is exactly ordered-pair interpolation, but their classification concerns classical matrix groups. Ordered-pair orbit preservation in Grech–Kisielewicz is the equivalent 2-closure viewpoint.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The natural action on group elements, not the faithful action on the vertices of a polygon or the action on reflections alone, is essential to the comparison.

evidence: 8d9ebcd5302a is a same-day classification of quantifier-rank-two first-order theories, not of two-local maps; 536f2a42ffb3 is a two-local classification for a finite-field affine Lie algebra.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Neither is a table or theorem giving the exact invariant of the dihedral action. A finite group-library census would not give this indexed all-n normal form unless it identifies the full ordered-pair action.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the full intransitive natural-action 2-closure, with mixed interpolation allowing independent choices of the rotation multiplier and the reflection permutation. The cyclic affine factor and tree order technology are not credited as new. In the inspected sources neither that full uncoupling nor its all-n consequence for the index is stated or supplied by a theorem specialized to this action.
residual_risks: Bounded comparison; an exact prior result under cyclic cyclotomic schemes or combined actions could have been missed.
Yu–Pan DOI 10.1515/math-2019-0063: DOI and publisher routes tried; full text unavailable. No inference of noncoverage from that access outcome.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete family calculation for two-point interpolation: it identifies precisely the independent choices responsible for local but nonglobal automorphisms and gives their exact excess for every modulus, including composite moduli and the two boundary groups. That answers more than finding an isolated counterexample or recomputing automorphism orders.
residual_risks: No claim of comparable closure behavior for noncyclic generalized dihedral groups.
